title: Variance of the identity under the Rademacher distribution
statement:
Let $X$ be a real random variable distributed according to the Rademacher distribution $\mathrm{Rad} = \tfrac12\delta_{-1} + \tfrac12\delta_{+1}$, so that $X$ takes the values $-1$ and $+1$ each with probability $1/2$. Then the variance of $X$ is
\[
\mathrm{Var}(X) = 1.
\]
hypotheses_covered: identity function as the random variable
replaced:
The variance of the identity function under the Rademacher distribution is $1$:
$\mathrm{Var}[\mathrm{id}; \mathrm{Rad}] = 1$.
